groups.name: Grammar
groups.description: Build simple, accurate sentences and understand everyday English.

items.title: Singular and plural nouns
items.can: I can talk about one thing or more than one.
items.example: one book / three books / two boxes
items.lesson: Add -s to most nouns and -es to words such as box.
items.assessment: Name six pictures, including singular and plural objects.

items.title: Irregular plurals
items.can: I can use special plural words.
items.example: one child / two children; one foot / two feet
items.lesson: Some plurals change: man → men, woman → women, mouse → mice, person → people. Sheep and fish can stay the same.
items.assessment: Name six pictures containing irregular plurals.

items.title: Countable and uncountable nouns
items.can: I can talk about things I can count and things I cannot count individually.
items.example: two apples / some rice / some water
items.lesson: Use numbers with countable things. Use some with food or drink like rice and milk.
items.assessment: Choose suitable expressions for six food pictures.

items.title: A, an and the
items.can: I can use small words before nouns.
items.example: a pencil / an egg / the door
items.lesson: Use a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound, and the when we know which thing.
items.assessment: Choose the correct article in six short sentences.

items.title: Some and numbers
items.can: I can say how many or how much in simple phrases.
items.example: three bananas / some bread / some pencils
items.lesson: Use a number with plural countable nouns. Use some for an unspecified amount or number.
items.assessment: Describe six groups of objects and foods.

items.title: This, that, these and those
items.can: I can point to things near me and far away.
items.example: This is a ball. / Those are trees.
items.lesson: This and that are for one thing; these and those are for more than one.
items.assessment: Identify six objects at different distances.

items.title: Subject pronouns
items.can: I can replace names with pronouns.
items.example: Tom is happy. → He is happy.
items.lesson: Use I, you, he, she, it, we and they to say who or what does something.
items.assessment: Replace six names or noun phrases with the right pronoun.

items.title: Object pronouns
items.can: I can understand who receives an action.
items.example: Look at her. / Can you help me?
items.lesson: Use me, you, him, her, it, us and them after verbs or prepositions.
items.assessment: Respond to six short picture-based prompts.

items.title: Possessive adjectives
items.can: I can say who something belongs to.
items.example: my bag / her shoes / their dog
items.lesson: Use my, your, his, her, its, our and their before a noun.
items.assessment: Describe ownership in six pictures.

items.title: Possessive pronouns
items.can: I can say whose thing it is without repeating the noun.
items.example: It is mine. / Is it yours?
items.lesson: Use mine, yours, his, hers, ours and theirs without another noun.
items.assessment: Identify the owners of five familiar objects.

items.title: Possessive ’s
items.can: I can show who owns something.
items.example: Sam’s bike / the girl’s hat
items.lesson: Add ’s to a name or singular noun to show ownership.
items.assessment: Describe ownership in five pictures.

items.title: One as a pronoun
items.can: I can use one instead of repeating a noun.
items.example: Which pencil? The red one.
items.lesson: Use one to refer to a single thing already mentioned.
items.assessment: Choose and describe objects from five pairs.

items.title: Adjectives
items.can: I can describe people and things.
items.example: a big dog / The dog is big.
items.lesson: Adjectives go before nouns or after be. They do not change for plural nouns.
items.assessment: Describe six objects using size, colour or another feature.

items.title: Be – affirmative
items.can: I can say who people are and describe them.
items.example: I am seven. / They are happy.
items.lesson: Use am with I, is with he/she/it and are with you/we/they. Practise I’m, she’s and they’re.
items.assessment: Make six descriptions using all three forms.

items.title: Be – negatives
items.can: I can say what something is not.
items.example: It isn’t red. / We aren’t sad.
items.lesson: Put not after am, is or are. Use isn’t and aren’t in everyday speech.
items.assessment: Correct five false picture descriptions.

items.title: Be – questions and short answers
items.can: I can ask and answer simple questions with be.
items.example: Is it blue? Yes, it is. / Are they happy? No, they aren’t.
items.lesson: Put am, is or are before the subject. Use the same verb in the short answer.
items.assessment: Ask and answer six picture questions.

items.title: Present simple – affirmative
items.can: I can talk about things I like and do.
items.example: I like bananas. / She plays tennis.
items.lesson: Use the base verb with I, you, we and they; usually add -s or -es with he, she and it.
items.assessment: Say three facts about yourself and three about another person.

items.title: Present simple – negatives
items.can: I can say what people do not like or do.
items.example: I don’t like eggs. / He doesn’t play hockey.
items.lesson: Use don’t or doesn’t plus the base verb.
items.assessment: Make six negative sentences about familiar activities or preferences.

items.title: Present simple – questions
items.can: I can ask and answer simple questions about habits and likes.
items.example: Do you like rice? Yes, I do. / Does she swim? No, she doesn’t.
items.lesson: Use do or does before the subject and the base verb after it.
items.assessment: Ask and answer six simple questions, including short answers.

items.title: Present continuous – affirmative
items.can: I can say what is happening now.
items.example: I’m drawing. / The boys are running.
items.lesson: Use am, is or are plus verb-ing. Notice run → running and make → making.
items.assessment: Describe six actions in a new picture.

items.title: Present continuous – negatives
items.can: I can say what is not happening now.
items.example: She isn’t sleeping. / They aren’t swimming.
items.lesson: Add not after am, is or are, before the -ing form.
items.assessment: Correct five inaccurate action descriptions.

items.title: Present continuous – questions
items.can: I can ask and answer questions about actions now.
items.example: What is he doing? He’s reading. / Are they playing? Yes, they are.
items.lesson: Put be before the subject; use verb-ing for the action.
items.assessment: Answer six questions about a new picture.

items.title: Present simple or continuous
items.can: I can distinguish a general fact from an action happening now.
items.example: I play tennis. / I’m playing tennis now.
items.lesson: Use present simple for habits and facts; use present continuous for actions happening now.
items.assessment: Choose the appropriate form for six simple situations.

items.title: Have got – possession
items.can: I can say what someone has or has not got.
items.example: I’ve got a bike. / She hasn’t got a kite.
items.lesson: Use have got or has got; negatives are haven’t got and hasn’t got. Have/has can also express possession.
items.assessment: Describe possessions in six pictures, including negatives.

items.title: Have got – questions
items.can: I can ask about possessions.
items.example: Have you got a pet? Yes, I have. / Has he got a ball?
items.lesson: Put have or has first, followed by the subject and got.
items.assessment: Ask and answer five questions about possessions.

items.title: Can and can’t – ability
items.can: I can talk about things I can and cannot do.
items.example: I can swim. / A fish can’t fly.
items.lesson: Use can or can’t followed by the base verb. It stays the same for every person.
items.assessment: Describe six abilities using can and can’t.

items.title: Can – questions and requests
items.can: I can ask about abilities and ask politely for something.
items.example: Can you run? Yes, I can. / Can I have a pencil, please?
items.lesson: Use can before the subject. For requests, add please.
items.assessment: Answer ability questions and make three polite requests.

items.title: Imperatives
items.can: I can understand and give simple instructions.
items.example: Stand up. / Don’t open the door.
items.lesson: Begin with the verb. Use don’t before it for a negative instruction.
items.assessment: Follow and give simple positive and negative instructions.

items.title: There is and there are
items.can: I can say what is in a place.
items.example: There is a cat. / There are three birds.
items.lesson: Use there is with one thing or an uncountable noun and there are with plural nouns.
items.assessment: Describe six details in a picture using both forms.

items.title: There is / are – questions and negatives
items.can: I can ask and say whether things are present.
items.example: Is there a bike? / There aren’t any dogs.
items.lesson: Put is or are first in questions. Add not for negatives.
items.assessment: Ask and answer five questions about a picture.

items.title: Prepositions of place
items.can: I can say where things are.
items.example: The ball is under the chair.
items.lesson: Practise in, on, under, behind, next to, between, in front of and at.
items.assessment: Place or identify objects in eight positions.

items.title: Time expressions
items.can: I can say when simple events happen.
items.example: in the morning / at night / today
items.lesson: Use in with morning, afternoon and evening; at with night. Practise today.
items.assessment: Match five activities to familiar times of day.

items.title: Question words – what and which
items.can: I can ask about things and choices.
items.example: What is this? / Which bag is yours?
items.lesson: What asks for information; which asks for a choice.
items.assessment: Answer and ask six questions about familiar objects.

items.title: Question words – who, whose and where
items.can: I can ask about people, ownership and places.
items.example: Who is she? / Whose bike is it? / Where is the cat?
items.lesson: Who asks about a person, whose about ownership and where about a place.
items.assessment: Answer six picture-based questions.

items.title: Question words – how
items.can: I can ask about number, age and spelling.
items.example: How many cats? / How old are you? / How do you spell it?
items.lesson: Use how many for countable objects, how old for age and how do you spell for letters.
items.assessment: Answer questions about quantities, age and spelling.

items.title: Adverbs and simple connectors
items.can: I can add details and join simple ideas.
items.example: Come here. / I’m drawing now. / I like cats and dogs.
items.lesson: Practise here, there, now, too, very, again and simple links such as and, but and or.
items.assessment: Complete and say six short sentences with appropriate words.

items.title: Like + -ing and -ing as a noun
items.can: I can name activities and say which I enjoy.
items.example: I like drawing. / Swimming is fun.
items.lesson: An -ing form can name an activity, including after like and as the subject of a sentence.
items.assessment: Say three activities you like and describe two activities.

items.title: Would like
items.can: I can politely say what I want or offer something.
items.example: I’d like an apple. / Would you like to play?
items.lesson: Use would like with a noun or to + verb. I’d is short for I would.
items.assessment: Make three requests or offers and respond politely.

items.title: Let’s – suggestions
items.can: I can suggest an activity.
items.example: Let’s play football.
items.lesson: Use let’s plus the base verb to suggest doing something together.
items.assessment: Suggest three activities in everyday situations.

items.title: Have + object + to-infinitive
items.can: I can understand simple phrases about something to do.
items.example: I have a picture to colour.
items.lesson: Use have + object + to + verb to describe a thing available for an activity.
items.assessment: Match and say four phrases about familiar things to do.

items.title: Everyday expressions
items.can: I can respond naturally in familiar situations.
items.example: Here you are. / Me too! / So do I. / What now?
items.lesson: Practise greetings, Happy birthday!, please, thank you, agreement and asking for the next instruction.
items.assessment: Respond appropriately in six short role-plays.

items.title: Exclamations and stories about activities
items.can: I can understand simple excited descriptions and story topics.
items.example: What a funny cat! / A story about riding a bike.
items.lesson: Use what + (a/an) + adjective + noun for exclamations; about + -ing for a story topic.
items.assessment: Make two exclamations and identify two story topics.

groups.name: Vocabulary
groups.description: Learn familiar words in manageable sets; practise recognition, recall and spelling.

items.title: Pets and farm animals
items.can: I can recognise and say words about pets and farm animals.
items.example: cat / dog / bird
items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Across short checks, identify and recall the words in this set from pictures or prompts. Write a selection without copying.

items.title: Wild animals and minibeasts
items.can: I can recognise and say words about wild animals and minibeasts.
items.example: elephant / tiger / giraffe
items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Across short checks, identify and recall the words in this set from pictures or prompts. Write a selection without copying.

items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Across short checks, identify and recall the words in this set from pictures or prompts. Write a selection without copying.

items.title: Numbers 1–10
items.can: I can recognise, say and write these numbers.
items.example: How many? ten.
items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Recognise the whole set and write five dictated numbers.

items.title: Numbers 11–20
items.can: I can recognise, say and write these numbers.
items.example: How many? twenty.
items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Recognise the whole set and write five dictated numbers.

items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Across short checks, identify and recall the words in this set from pictures or prompts. Write a selection without copying.

items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Across short checks, identify and recall the words in this set from pictures or prompts. Write a selection without copying.

items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Across short checks, identify and recall the words in this set from pictures or prompts. Write a selection without copying.

items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Across short checks, identify and recall the words in this set from pictures or prompts. Write a selection without copying.

items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Across short checks, identify and recall the words in this set from pictures or prompts. Write a selection without copying.

items.title: Furniture and home objects
items.can: I can recognise and say words about furniture and home objects.
items.example: bed / chair / armchair
items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Across short checks, identify and recall the words in this set from pictures or prompts. Write a selection without copying.

items.title: School and classroom

items.example: school / classroom / teacher
items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Across short checks, identify and recall the words in this set from pictures or prompts. Write a selection without copying.

items.title: Toys and games
items.can: I can recognise and say words about toys and games.
items.example: toy / doll / teddy bear
items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Across short checks, identify and recall the words in this set from pictures or prompts. Write a selection without copying.

items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Across short checks, identify and recall the words in this set from pictures or prompts. Write a selection without copying.

items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Across short checks, identify and recall the words in this set from pictures or prompts. Write a selection without copying.

items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Across short checks, identify and recall the words in this set from pictures or prompts. Write a selection without copying.

items.title: Actions and movement

items.example: run / walk / jump
items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Across short checks, identify and recall the words in this set from pictures or prompts. Write a selection without copying.

items.title: Everyday and classroom verbs
items.can: I can recognise and say words about everyday and classroom verbs.
items.example: eat / drink / sleep
items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Across short checks, identify and recall the words in this set from pictures or prompts. Write a selection without copying.

items.title: Adjectives and feelings
items.can: I can recognise and say words about adjectives and feelings.
items.example: big / small / long
items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Across short checks, identify and recall the words in this set from pictures or prompts. Write a selection without copying.

items.title: Time and special days
items.can: I can recognise and say words about time and special days.
items.example: morning / afternoon / evening
items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Across short checks, identify and recall the words in this set from pictures or prompts. Write a selection without copying.

items.title: Positions and directions
items.can: I can recognise and say words about positions and directions.
items.example: in / on / under
items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Across short checks, identify and recall the words in this set from pictures or prompts. Write a selection without copying.

items.title: The alphabet
items.can: I can recognise, say and write the letters of the alphabet.
items.example: A – B – C / How do you spell it?
items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Recognise all letters in mixed order and write ten dictated letters.

items.title: Spelling first names
items.can: I can recognise familiar names and spell them when I hear the letters.
items.example: My name is Sam. S-A-M.
items.lesson: Practise recognising the spoken word, saying it and reading it. Use the word in a short phrase where possible.
items.assessment: Match familiar spoken names and write five dictated names.

groups.name: Reading & writing
groups.description: Read familiar English, spell words and practise all five paper-based Starters tasks.

items.title: Recognise written words
items.can: I can match familiar written words to pictures.
items.example: dog → a picture of a dog
items.lesson: Read the whole word and check the first and last letters.
items.assessment: Match ten written words to pictures.

items.title: Spell familiar words independently
items.can: I can write familiar words without copying.
items.example: cat / pencil / banana
items.lesson: Say the word, think of its sounds and letters, then check your spelling.
items.assessment: Write ten familiar picture words without a model.

items.title: Read and understand simple sentences
items.can: I can understand short sentences about familiar things.
items.example: The cat is on the bed.
items.lesson: Find the person or object, action and other details.
items.assessment: Match six short sentences to pictures.

items.title: Read simple questions
items.can: I can understand questions about a picture.
items.example: What colour is the bag? / Where is the dog?
items.lesson: Look at the question word first to work out what information is needed.
items.assessment: Choose suitable answers to six questions.

items.title: Part 1 – match sentences to pictures
items.can: I can decide whether a short sentence matches a picture.
items.example: These are pencils. → ✓ or ✗
items.lesson: Check the object and whether there is one or more than one.
items.assessment: Complete a five-question Part 1-style task.

items.title: Part 2 – write yes or no
items.can: I can read descriptions of a scene and decide if they are true.
items.example: The boy is eating. → yes / no
items.lesson: Check the whole sentence against the picture and write yes or no.
items.assessment: Complete a five-question Part 2-style task.

items.title: Part 3 – put letters in order
items.can: I can spell picture words using mixed-up letters.
items.example: t a c → cat
items.lesson: Name the pictured object, arrange the letters and check that every letter is used.
items.assessment: Complete a five-word Part 3-style task.

items.title: Part 4 – complete a short text
items.can: I can choose missing nouns from a picture word bank.
items.example: A rabbit has two long ___. → ears
items.lesson: Read the words around the gap, choose a noun that makes sense and copy it accurately.
items.assessment: Complete a five-gap Part 4-style task.

items.title: Part 5 – answer picture-story questions
items.can: I can follow a picture story and write a one-word answer.
items.example: What is the girl holding? → ball
items.lesson: Look at all three pictures, read each question and write one correct word.
items.assessment: Complete a five-question Part 5-style task.

items.title: Copy words accurately
items.can: I can copy words without missing or changing letters.
items.example: elephant → elephant
items.lesson: Compare the copied word with the model, letter by letter.
items.assessment: Copy eight words accurately from a word bank.

groups.name: Speaking & listening
groups.description: Understand short conversations and instructions; practise all paper-based listening and speaking tasks.

items.title: Greetings and personal information
items.can: I can greet someone and give my name and age.
items.example: Hello! I’m Alex. I’m eight.
items.lesson: Practise answering naturally, without memorising a long speech.
items.assessment: Respond to greetings and answer name and age questions.

items.title: Follow simple classroom instructions
items.can: I can understand short spoken instructions.
items.example: Open your book. / Point to the door.
items.lesson: Listen for the action, object and location.
items.assessment: Follow six spoken instructions without translation.

items.title: Listening Part 1 – match names to people
items.can: I can identify a person from a spoken description.
items.example: Ben is the boy with the green bag.
items.lesson: Listen to the name and all the details before drawing a line.
items.assessment: Complete a five-question matching task with two listens.

items.title: Listening Part 2 – write names and numbers
items.can: I can listen and write a name or number.
items.example: S-A-M → Sam / fourteen → 14
items.lesson: Listen for each letter or number, then check your answer on the second listen.
items.assessment: Complete a five-question note-taking task with two listens.

items.title: Listening Part 3 – choose the correct picture
items.can: I can identify specific information in a short conversation.
items.example: Which animal does she like?
items.lesson: Look at the three pictures first, then listen for the detail that distinguishes them.
items.assessment: Complete a five-question picture-choice task with two listens.

items.title: Listening Part 4 – colour the correct objects
items.can: I can follow spoken colour and position instructions.
items.example: Colour the ball next to the chair blue.
items.lesson: Find the right object by its position, then listen for its colour.
items.assessment: Complete a five-question colouring task with two listens.

items.title: Speaking Part 1 – point and place cards
items.can: I can identify objects and put cards in the right place.
items.example: Point to the tree. / Put the fish under the table.
items.lesson: Listen to the object and position, then point or move the card.
items.assessment: Identify objects in a scene and place three cards as instructed.

items.title: Speaking Part 2 – answer scene questions
items.can: I can answer questions about objects, colours, numbers and actions.
items.example: How many ducks are there? / What is she doing?
items.lesson: Look at the part of the picture the examiner indicates. Give a clear short answer.
items.assessment: Answer six questions about a new scene.

items.title: Speaking Part 2 – tell me about it
items.can: I can say something simple about a person or object.
items.example: It’s red. It’s on the chair.
items.lesson: Use a colour, size, position or action to add a detail.
items.assessment: Give relevant information about three pictured objects.

items.title: Speaking Part 3 – answer object-card questions
items.can: I can identify an object and answer a related question.
items.example: What is it? A bike. / Have you got a bike? Yes.
items.lesson: Name the object, then listen to the follow-up question about it.
items.assessment: Answer questions on four different object cards.

items.title: Speaking Part 4 – answer personal questions
items.can: I can talk briefly about my family, school and favourite things.
items.example: My favourite sport is tennis. / I have one brother.
items.lesson: Listen to the question word and give a relevant answer. Short answers are fine.
items.assessment: Answer six varied personal questions without a script.

items.title: Ask for repetition
items.can: I can ask someone to say something again.
items.example: Sorry? / Again, please.
items.lesson: If you do not understand, ask politely rather than staying silent.
items.assessment: Use an appropriate request in two role-play situations.

items.title: Clear pronunciation
items.can: I can say familiar words clearly enough to be understood.
items.example: three / green / shoes
items.lesson: Listen to a model, repeat the word and pay attention to its sounds and stress.
items.assessment: Say familiar words and short answers intelligibly in a conversation.
